interactions.note: The epitope of nanobody Nb39 on the kappa-opioid receptor (KOR) bound to the G protein-biased agonist nalfurafine was determined from the crystal structure of the complex. Nanobody Nb39 was used as a G protein mimetic to stabilize the active conformation of KOR. The human KOR construct replaced the N-terminal residues 1-53 with a thermostabilized apocytochrome b562RIL (BRIL) 1-106 peptide, with a glycine-serine linker, to increase receptor expression, and to facilitate crystallization.; Unmapped quantitative response: 3D structure 3.3 angstroms

The epitope of nanobody Nb39 on the kappa-opioid receptor (KOP) bound to the epoxymorphinan opioid agonist MP1104 was determined from the crystal structure of the complex. Nanobody Nb39 was used as a G protein mimetic to stabilize the active conformation of KOP.  The human KOP construct used an N-terminal thermostabilized apocytochrome b562RIL (BRIL) to increase receptor expression, and to facilitate crystallization. There are two complexes in the asymmetric unit.; Unmapped quantitative response: 3D structure 3.1 angstroms

The epitope of negative allosteric nanobody Nb6 on the kappa-opioid receptor (KOR), bound to the inverse agonist JDTic, was determined from the crystal structure of the complex. The human KOR fusion construct used an N-terminal thermostabilized apocytochrome b562RIL (BRIL) to increase receptor expression, and to facilitate crystallization. The antagonist JDTic36 afforded maximal stabilization of the KOR–Nb6 complex. There are two complexes in the asymmetric unit.; Unmapped quantitative response: 3D structure 3.3 angstroms
